correctness.rationale: The full proof establishes an embedded theta-ary witness for any late excitation by nonbacktracking spatial dependence and the refractory two-step exclusion. On a forest each selected causal branch is disjoint. The matching leaf-to-root pulse attains the tree-specific clock, and counting minimal witnesses plus silent pendant extension attains the n-only bound. Exhaustive checks cover 1,882,829 exact initial states over 241 graph-parameter cases, with an independent 8,896-case constructive checker. The proof, not finite experiments, establishes all n, theta and kappa.

evidence: Bello–Sivakoff arXiv:2108.06404, Lemma 2.7(ii): no excitement after rooted depth plus one, and all rest by depth plus kappa.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The finite-tree depth bound gives an upper bound that is not sharp on long paths (the new fixed-forest clock is kappa). The density budget applies on arbitrary sparse graphs but does not give the exact maximal time and can scale with n; a stronger domain does not mean stronger conclusions. Neither result implies the exact arbitrary-forest branching-rank equality or universal attained n-only logarithmic law.

value.rationale: Determines the exact worst-case rest time on every finite forest from a natural branching invariant computable by messages. Gives a sharp, attained logarithmic universal law and identifies a structural causal reason why thresholds >=2 differ from single-contact propagation. Earlier depth and event-budget bounds are nonsharp; the improvement is substantial on long paths and stars. Complete natural classification, not an arbitrary small-graph computation.
